title: seed-default-cost-curves-and-quant-sanity-runner
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduces tenant-level default cost curve seeder to accelerate on-boarding
Adds a CLI runner that runs lightweight quantization sanity sweeps and reports cost/quality deltas
Telemetry hooks to track per-tenant unit-econ estimates and seeding outcomes
Rollout gated behind feature flag and can be rolled back without data migration
description: Motivation: Many customers spend engineering time manually tuning batching, cache and quantization presets for cost/latency targets. This PR introduces an automated "seeder" and a small CLI "sanity runner" that together generate conservative default cost-curves and candidate quant profiles for new tenants and for periodic re-evaluation. Scope: 1) econ seeder service that synthesizes tenant default profiles (batch size targets, cache TTL hints, quant candidate list) based on recent traffic shape or a lightweight synthetic sampler; 2) a quant-sanity CLI that runs controlled micro-benchmarks across a small set of quant candidates (int8, 4-bit q* variants) and reports quality regressions with token-level diffs and unit-econ delta; 3) telemetry and metrics (seed.outcome, quant.sanity.quality_delta, econ.estimated_unit_cost) and a rollout feature flag; 4) small UX additions in Console to preview seeded defaults and accept/reject. Implementation notes: seeder is implemented in Go under pkg/econ with a strategy pipeline: sample -> profile -> conservative-curve generator. The quant sanity runner is a thin Python harness (tools/quant_sanity) that invokes the runtime's deterministic inference api and compares top-k and logprobs to a reference model. The CLI can be run in dry-run mode to produce JSON diffs. Testing and safety: seeding defaults are intentionally conservative and include a "safety multiplier" that prevents aggressive batch increases. We added e2e smoke tests that run the CLI on a synthetic tenant and verify telemetry emission. Rollout: feature flag redwood.econ.default-seeder controls both seeding and the Console preview; we'll rollout to internal tenants first. Related: ENG-5142 tracks follow-ups to expose per-tenant CLI scheduling and to add an opt-out API for security-sensitive customers. Checklist: - [x] design doc and telemetry spec linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] e2e smoke + CI job - [x] Console preview wiring - [x] feature-flag gating - [x] docs stub for runbook and rollback Flow of commits and what changed: see commits list.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can we add a short timeout for the quant-sanity runner to avoid long CLI jobs? (suggest 30s per candidate)
Priya Shah: Added a timeout flag to the CLI with default 25s and a CI test to validate it doesn't regress wall time
Marta Ivanov: Safety question — how do we prevent the seeder from suggesting changes that violate tenant SLAs?
Priya Shah: Seeder applies SLA-aware constraints; added a 'sla_override' guard which requires explicit opt-in and is off by default
Jun Park: Minor nit: prefer smaller exported function surface in pkg/econ; propose moving helper ValidateProfile to internal/validation
Priya Shah: Moved ValidateProfile to internal/validation and updated call sites; all unit tests green
qa_notes: How tested: local seeding with synthetic tenant, CI e2e smoke, telemetry verified in staging cluster
Edge cases: extremely bursty tenants will fallback to conservative defaults; seeder will not reduce cache TTL below a tenant-specific minimum
Rollback: disable redwood.econ.default-seeder feature flag and revert Console preview (no DB migrations)
merge_outcome: Merged by squash commit via GitHub UI. Squash commit message: "econ: seed conservative default cost curves + add quant sanity CLI". No post-merge migration required. Feature gated behind redwood.econ.default-seeder.
notes_for_operators: Monitor metric: seeder.success_rate (expect >95% on synthetic traffic)
Alert if quant.sanity.quality_delta > 0.05 for more than 5 tenants in 1h
If rollout causes regressions, flip feature flag to disable seeding and follow runbook in docs/runbooks/econ-seeder.md
